title: Team Readiness Broker and Dependency SLA
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Cross-functional roadmap dependencies (Engineering, Design, Security, Infra) routinely result in late gate handoffs, unclear acceptance criteria, and last-minute escalations that delay launches and increase incident risk. Objective: Build a 'Team Readiness Broker' — a lightweight coordination layer and SLA scheme that codifies readiness signals, automates preflight checks, and provides visible escalation paths so teams can sign-off on downstream readiness well before cutover windows. Goals:
- Define dependency SLAs (e.g., sign-off windows, response time, review cadence) for cross-team handoffs tied to cycle milestones.
- Create a readiness schema with checklist items per domain (Design review, API contract, infra capacity, security review, e2e smoke).
- Implement an observable readiness dashboard that surfaces gating status and predicted blocker risk for product managers and release owners.
- Provide automated reminders, a lightweight broker workflow (Linear + GitHub + Confluence links), and a runbook for when SLAs are missed.
Success criteria (MVP):
1) Readiness schema defined and approved by Eng, Design, Security, Infra.
2) Automated readiness checks implemented for 3 pilot initiatives and integrated into Linear tickets.
3) Dashboard showing per-initiative readiness score with historical SLA adherence.
4) Runbook + escalation policy published and exercised during two release gates.
Deliverables:
- Readiness schema document (Confluence) with domain checklists and acceptance criteria.
- Linear ticket templates and custom fields for readiness state.
- Small backend to aggregate signals (webhooks from GitHub checks, PR status, security sign-off label, infra capacity flag).
- Visibility dashboard (Console or Grafana) and alerting rules for SLA breaches.
- Runbook and postmortem template for missed SLAs.
Non-goals for MVP: full enforcement blocking merges, heavyweight vendor integrations, retrofitting historical initiatives.
Privacy & compliance notes: security sign-offs must not expose secrets; integrations should respect existing KMS/HSM boundaries for private deployments.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams treat broker as checkbox, not coordination tool. Mitigation: require at least one synchronous gating meeting per initiative and include SLA penalty-free 'learning' period.
Risk: False positives/negatives from automated checks (e.g., PR status stale). Mitigation: include manual verification step in schema and ensure webhook retries + webhook health metrics.
Risk: Overhead for small initiatives. Mitigation: provide opt-out flag for micro-features and clear criteria for when full readiness applies.
